extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, counsel and parties participating in PTAB proceedings (petitioners, patent owners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and glossary of procedural rules, filing requirements, evidentiary standards, and formatting for PTAB proceedings (IPR, PGR, CBM). Intended to help practitioners prepare petitions, motions, responses, and manage trials before the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter voir dire and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Voir dire of the Interpreter is not required, but the parties must make any objections to the Interpreter’s qualifications at the time of the testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same Interpreter may be used for depositions and to prepare the witness. The opposing party may only inquire into whether the Interpreter helped prepare the witness but not the substance of the preparations. (Ariosa Diagnostics v. Isis Innovation Ltd., IPR2012-00022, Paper 67)

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Accused infringer’s rights to avoid infringement for previously lawful activity that later becomes unlawful when claims are substantively amended during a PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervening Rights may exist for any amended or new claims determined patentable and incorporated into a patent during an IPR, PGR or CBM. 35 U.S.C. § 318(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent or any of its claims do not comply with prerequisites in 35 U.S.C., the patent or its claims are invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB does not presume validity; petitioner bears a lower burden (preponderance) than in district court (clear and convincing). See Standard of Proof entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity, Standard of Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: District court: rebuttable presumption of validity; invalidation requires Clear and Convincing Evidence. PTAB: no presumption; invalidity established by Preponderance of the Evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: 35 U.S.C. § 282 (district court); 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.1(d), 42.20(c) (PTAB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder (motions and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination of a second PTAB Proceeding with a first, already-instituted proceeding. Both Patent Owner and Petitioner may request Joinder by Motion, filed no later than one month after Instituting the first PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB will grant Joinder only if the second petition warrants institution and the Patent Owner’s Preliminary Response has been submitted or the time to do so has expired. One Year Bar does not apply to concurrently filed petitions with a Motion for Joinder. 37 C.F.R. § 42.122.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Petitioners — single voice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Group of distinct entities filing a single Petition is treated as a single party that must speak with a single voice in writing and oral representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual arguments, submissions or sections in consolidated filings are not allowed. Only one Lead Counsel is permitted for Joint Petitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment (Final Written Decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB’s Final Written Decision disposing of all issues that were, or reasonably could have been, raised and decided during a PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Final Written Decision may be designated precedential or informative as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line Spacing and Spacing (formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Double spacing must be used for filings except certain items; block quotes may be 1.5 spaced and must be indented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double spacing except for Claim Charts, headings, tables of contents, tables of authorities, indices, signature blocks, and certificates of service. Block quotations may be 1.5 spaced but indented from both left and right. 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(a)(2); 42.6(2)(iii). See Petition, Formatting of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Initial Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree to Mandatory Initial Disclosures per the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide; agreement must be submitted by Patent Owner Preliminary Response filing or expiration of that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon Institution, parties may automatically take Discovery of information identified in Mandatory Initial Disclosures. If parties fail to agree, a party may seek disclosures by Motion. 37 C.F.R. § 42.51(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Notices (who must disclose what and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Petitioner and Patent Owner must file: (1) identification of each Real Party-in-Interest, (2) identification of related matters, (3) identification of Lead and Back-up Counsel, and (4) identification of service information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must file notices with the Petition; Patent Owner must file within 21 days of service of the Petition. Both must file updated notices within 21 days of changes. 37 C.F.R. § 42.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins (formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents filed in a PTAB Proceeding must have page margins of at least 2.5 centimeters (1 inch) on all sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(2)(iv). See Petition, Formatting of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion (contents and authorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Motion is a request for relief other than by Petition and must include precise relief requested and a full statement of reasons; may include a statement of material facts. 37 C.F.R. § 42.22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, PTAB requires authorization before filing most Motions (conference call with parties) and Motions will not be entered without authorization. Exceptions: Motions to Seal and Motions filed with Petitions do not require prior authorization. Some Motions (Rehearing, to Exclude Evidence, for Observation on Cross-Examination) require authorization but may be automatically granted. 37 C.F.R. § 42.20(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion Filing Schedule and default response times
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions may only be filed according to PTAB-set schedule. Default times: Opposition due one month after service; Reply due one month after service of Opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for Observation on Cross-Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion to draw PTAB’s attention to relevant cross-examination testimony of a reply witness; no further substantive paper permitted after Reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation must be a concise statement of relevance of precisely identified testimony to a precisely identified argument or exhibit portion; should not exceed a single short paragraph. Patent Owner may respond equally concisely and specifically. See Office Patent Trial Practice Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Amend (timing and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Motion by Patent Owner to seek Claim Amendment. May be filed only after Institution and after conferring with the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If granted, proposed Substitute Claims are added to the patent without Examination. 37 C.F.R. § 42.121. Motions to Amend are limited to 25 pages and may include a claim appendix that does not count toward page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Exclude Evidence (contents and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion challenging admissibility (not sufficiency) of Evidence. Must explain why evidence is not admissible and: (1) identify where objection was originally made, (2) identify where in record evidence was relied upon by opponent, (3) address objections to exhibits in numerical order, (4) explain each objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Motion to Exclude must be filed to preserve objections; PTAB may not resolve until filed. No prior PTAB authorization required. Objections preserved by such motions in Preliminary Proceeding must be served within 10 business days of Institution; after Institution, within five business days of service of the Evidence. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.64(b)(1), 42.64(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Expunge Confidential Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion filed after denial of a Petition or after entry of Final Written Decision to remove confidential information from the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB is under no obligation to grant such Motions. 37 C.F.R. § 42.56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Seal (good cause standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion to prevent information from becoming public record. Filing party must establish good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must show information is truly confidential and confidentiality outweighs strong public interest in open record. Potentially confidential info includes exhibits, transcripts, papers and decisions alleged to contain trade secrets or other confidential commercial info. 37 C.F.R. § 42.54.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Strike
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion to remove all or part of a piece of Evidence or submitted paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Motion to Exclude is typically the proper procedure to remove Evidence. 37 C.F.R. § 42.64(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Terminate (joint request and PTAB discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may jointly request termination of a PTAB Proceeding before Final Written Decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB is not required to grant termination and may proceed to Final Written Decision without a Petitioner; PTAB has sole discretion. 35 U.S.C. §§ 317, 327; 37 C.F.R. § 42.72.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation to Combine (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Obviousness, there needs to be a reason, suggestion, or motivation in the prior art that would lead a person of ordinary skill to combine references and suggest a reasonable likelihood of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement guards against hindsight bias in Obviousness determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (35 U.S.C. § 102)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention cannot be patented if it was patented, described in a Printed Publication, in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Prior Use, Prior Sale, Printed Publication; 35 U.S.C. § 102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections, Timing of
rubrics_metrics.description: Objection to Evidence during Preliminary Proceeding must be served within 10 business days of Institution (except deposition evidence must be objected during deposition). After Trial Instituted, objections must be served within five business days of Evidence’s service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness (35 U.S.C. § 103 and Graham factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may not issue if claimed invention differences from prior art make the claimed invention obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art. Courts consider Graham factors when determining Obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer for Sale / Sale (prior art/defense)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer for Sale: a definite offer the acceptance of which would create a binding contract by simple acceptance. Sale: transfer of commercial embodiment for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both can trigger invalidity if before the one-year statutory bar. See 35 U.S.C. § 102 and Prior Sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Patent Trial Practice Guide (reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guide published by PTO regarding Trial practice in PTAB Proceedings (37 C.F.R. Part 42).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides foundational procedural guidance referenced throughout the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: One Year Bar / Statutory Bar (35 U.S.C. § 315(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IPR may not be Instituted if Petition is filed more than one year after the Petitioner, RPI, or privy is served with a patent infringement complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are exceptions (e.g., joinder filed concurrently). 35 U.S.C. § 315(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to a Motion (contents and deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition must include: (1) statement of precise relief requested, (2) full statement of reasons for relief requested, and (3) statement identifying material facts in dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Opposition is due one month after service of the Motion and has same Page Limit as the Motion. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.23, 42.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary and Customary Meaning / Plain Meaning (claim construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim terms are given the meaning they would have to a person of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention, based on the entire record (intrinsic and extrinsic evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes patent claims, specification, prosecution history, and extrinsic evidence like dictionaries and expert reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Limits (document length limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on number of pages for Petitions, Motions, responses and Oppositions, excluding certain front/back matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions requesting IPR: 60 pages. Petitions requesting PGR or CBM: 80 pages. Petitions requesting DERs: 60 pages. Motions: 15 pages. Patent Owner Preliminary Responses, Patent Owner Responses and Oppositions to a Motion have same limits as corresponding Petitions/Motions. Replies to Patent Owner Responses: 25 pages. Replies to Oppositions to a Motion: 5 pages. Proposed 2015 rule change would replace with word counts (e.g., 14,000 words for IPR petitions). 37 C.F.R. § 42.24(a)-(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner Preliminary Response (purpose and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before Institution, Patent Owner may file an initial response to a Petition setting forth reasons why Trial should not be Instituted. 37 C.F.R. § 42.107.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rule change would allow testimonial evidence (declaration) with Preliminary Response (Aug 20, 2015 proposal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner Response (post-institution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Response by Patent Owner to address any Ground of Invalidity not already rejected by Institution Decision. Due three months from Institution unless PTAB orders otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Owner typically submits testimonial evidence (declaration) with the Response. Page limits same as Petition. 37 C.F.R. § 42.120.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process of applying for a patent: drafting, filing, communicating with PTO examiner, and potentially amending claims to establish patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct from patent litigation and PTAB Proceedings, which occur after prosecution and issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) (role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutorily created administrative board within the PTO that presides over PTAB Proceedings, appeals from examiner decisions, and replaced the BPAI after AIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes APJs who render decisions on PTAB Proceedings and Interferences. 35 U.S.C. § 6(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable Subject Matter (35 U.S.C. § 101 limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be patentable, claimed invention must be directed to a process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter and not wholly directed to laws of nature, physical phenomena, abstract ideas, or other judicially recognized exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground of Invalidity available in CBM and PGR. See 2014 Interim Guidance on Patent Subject Matter Eligibility. 35 U.S.C. § 101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency (statutory time limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: After Institution, a PTAB Proceeding is normally pending no more than one year; can be extended up to six months for good cause or adjusted for Joinder. 37 C.F.R. § 42.200(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling Orders set deadlines to ensure completion within statutory pendency while accounting for complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending Civil Action (relationship to PTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: District court litigation involving same patent pending in PTAB Proceeding; parties often seek a Stay of Litigation until PTAB concludes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related Matters and disclosures required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for the PTAB to Institute a PTAB Trial. 37 C.F.R. § 42.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must meet statutory and regulatory requirements; must comply with Petition Formatting and Page Limit requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition, Content of (statutory and regulatory requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory: (1) identify all Real Parties-in-Interest, (2) identify all challenged claims and all Grounds of Invalidity, (3) provide copies of Evidence relied upon, and (4) pay filing fee. 35 U.S.C. § 312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory: (1) identify grounds for standing, (2) propose Claim Construction for each challenged claim, (3) specifically explain Grounds of Invalidity, and (4) specifically explain relevance of Evidence relied upon. 37 C.F.R. § 42.22(a)(2). IPR petitions must also set forth grounds for standing and provide precise identification of relief requested for each challenged claim and supporting exhibits. 37 C.F.R. § 42.104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition Formatting (font, margins, spacing, page size)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must use page size 8.5 x 11 inches except exhibits requiring larger size. Markings must be black or equivalent high-contrast; fonts must be proportional 14-point or monospaced no more than 4 characters/cm; double spacing used except certain items; margins at least 2.5 cm (1 inch). 37 C.F.R. § 42.6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See specific exemptions for claim charts, headings, tables of contents, tables of authorities, indices, signature blocks and certificates of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Party filing a Petition requesting a Trial be Instituted. 37 C.F.R. § 42.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must file Mandatory Notices with the Petition including Real Parties-in-Interest and Related Matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phillips Standard (claim construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim construction standard used in federal district court: words given their ordinary and customary meaning as understood by a person of ordinary skill in the art at time of invention, per Phillips v. AWH Corp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in district courts; PTAB may apply different standards depending on proceeding and claim construction proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Grant Review (PGR) scope and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB Proceeding to request cancelling claims on Grounds including Novelty, Obviousness, Written Description, Enablement, Indefiniteness and Patentable Subject Matter. All prior art available including Prior Sale and Prior Use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition for PGR not instituted if Petitioner previously filed declaratory judgment challenging patent validity. PGR only for first-to-file patents within nine months after issuance. 35 U.S.C. § 321(b); 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.201-42.204.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of Attorney (when required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must file written document authorizing practitioners or joint inventors to act on their behalf when designating counsel. 37 C.F.R. § 1.32(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Owner should not file additional POA if designated counsel is already counsel of record in PTAB Proceeding. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedential and Informative Opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Precedential Opinion: Final Written Decision binding on the PTAB when majority of APJs vote to designate. Informative Decisions: not binding but illustrate PTAB norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation affects future panels and public guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Proceeding (phase description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase beginning with filing a Petition and ending with an Institution Decision. 37 C.F.R. § 42.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain timing rules for objections, supplemental information, and preliminary responses apply to this phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preponderance of the Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard of Proof required to establish a patent’s Invalidity in PTAB Proceedings; must show it is more likely than not that the patent is invalid. 37 C.F.R. § 42.1(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower burden than Clear and Convincing Evidence used in district court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary and Secondary References (for combining prior art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary Reference: discloses many claim elements and may be combined with Secondary Reference(s) to show Obviousness. Secondary Reference(s): disclose other claim elements to be combined with Primary Reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when alleging combination grounds; see Motivation to Combine guidance to avoid hindsight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed Publication (as prior art)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference publicly disseminated or otherwise made available so it can be located and accessed by persons of ordinary skill exercising reasonable diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to establish novelty or anticipation under §102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Sale (anticipation / statutory bar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial sale more than one year before patent application filing can invalidate a patent; may be raised in PGR or CBM but not in IPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Sale and 35 U.S.C. § 102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Use (anticipation / statutory bar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Good faith public use more than one year before filing can invalidate a patent; applies to commercial and non-profit uses if public is intended beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be raised in PGR or CBM but not in IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority (effective filing date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Date on which inventor established a right to patent — generally effective filing date; in multijurisdictional filings, applicant may claim priority within 12 months under WIPO conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects novelty and prior art determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy / Real Party-in-Interest (disclosure and inquiry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Real Party-in-Interest: party who desires institution — typically petitioner or controlling party; determination is fact-dependent (control, funding, direction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must disclose all Real Parties-in-Interest as part of Mandatory Notices. Office Patent Trial Practice Guide factors include funding, direction, or control. 37 C.F.R. § 42.8(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro Hac Vice admission (requirements and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsel may be admitted pro hac vice in a PTAB Proceeding even if not a registered practitioner; Motion must be filed more than 21 days after service of the Petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition due within one week; no Reply permitted. Motion must include statement of good cause and Declaration attesting to bar standing, no suspensions/disbarments, no prior denials, no sanctions/contempt, that counsel will read practice guide and rules, will be subject to PTO Code, and has familiarity with subject matter; list other PTO pro hac vice admissions in last three years. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10; see Motorola Mobility v. Arnouse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Protective Order (when submitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may submit a Proposed Protective Order that differs from Default Protective Order, explaining differences and compliance with Practice Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often submitted with a Motion to Seal; opposing party may access filed information by agreeing to terms. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.54, 42.55.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective Order (purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement between PTAB and parties identifying confidential information and governing disclosure rules among parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default Protective Order exists; parties can propose alternatives per rules. 37 C.F.R. § 42.54.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Proceeding (definition and common types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Litigation-like process under the AIA for challenging validity of issued patents. Common proceedings include CBM review, IPR, and PGR. Begins with filing a Petition; Trial period begins at Institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial pendency statutorily limited to one year after Institution, with extensions for good cause. 37 C.F.R. § 42.2; § 42.200(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable Likelihood Standard (for IPR institution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discretionary standard requiring Petitioner to establish it is more likely than not to prevail as to at least one Ground of Invalidity for IPR Institution. 35 U.S.C. § 314(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different from showing invalidity by preponderance at trial; threshold for institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundant Grounds of Invalidity (horizontal & vertical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds that are the same or substantially the same as those in a previous petition will not be considered. PTAB classifies redundancy as Horizontal or Vertical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB will not sustain more than one Ground of Invalidity per claim unless Petitioner explains why multiple grounds are not redundant. If a ground is rejected for redundancy, petitioner is estopped from pursuing it later. Petitioners should choose strongest grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Matters (disclosure requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other judicial or administrative matter that would affect or be affected by a PTAB decision (e.g., Pending Civil Action, related patent applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Petitioner must disclose all Related Matters in Mandatory Notices. 37 C.F.R. § 42.8(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply (definition and use)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party’s response to any Petition, Motion or Opposition filed by opposing party in a PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply deadlines and page limits vary by document type. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.23, 42.24(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Adverse Judgment (what it can include)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party’s request for judgment against itself, including disclaimer, cancellation/disclaimer of claims leaving no claims at trial, concession of unpatentability or derivation, or abandonment of PTAB Proceeding. 37 C.F.R. § 42.73(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically used after acquisition, change in privy, or where owner does not want joinder risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Rehearing / Reconsideration (requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to reconsider PTAB’s decision on a Petition or Motion; need not obtain prior authorization but must specifically identify matters believed misapprehended or overlooked and where each matter was previously addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request to Rehear a Petition for Institution must be filed within 30 days of Institution Decision. 37 C.F.R. § 42.71(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine Discovery and Additional Discovery standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine Discovery: exhibits cited in papers/testimony, cross-examination of affidavit testimony, and relevant information inconsistent with party positions; in IPR, Additional Discovery requires showing necessity in interest of justice; in PGR/CBM, additional discovery may be granted for good cause and limited to evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 11 Certification (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed 2015 rule change to add a Rule 11-type certification for all papers filed and sanctions for noncompliance applying to practitioners and parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Was proposed on Aug 20, 2015; not necessarily in force at time of guide text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling Order (content and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Order issued with Institution Decision setting due dates for an instituted trial, considering complexity while ensuring trial completes within one-year statutory pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice Guide for Proposed Trial Rules guidance (77 Fed. Reg. 6868, 6869).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary Considerations (objective evidence against obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective evidence tending to show invention was not obvious over asserted prior art — e.g., commercial success, industry recognition, long-felt need, unexpected results, copying by competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as part of Obviousness analysis in IPR, PGR, CBM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary Reference (prior art combination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference(s) that disclose other claim elements to be combined with a Primary Reference to show Obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies role of multiple references in combination arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement (effect on PTAB proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement between parties that can form basis for Motion to Terminate, but PTAB not required to terminate and may proceed to Final Written Decision regardless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak with a Single Voice (Unified/Consolidated cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Unified Cases involving Joint Petitioners or Consolidation, multiple Petitioners are a single party and must strictly speak with a single voice in writing and oral representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual arguments/submissions in consolidated filings are not allowed; only one Lead Counsel may represent multiple Joint Petitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of Proof (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Level of evidence required depends on issue, motion, and proceeding; two applicable standards are Clear and Convincing Evidence and Preponderance of the Evidence. 35 U.S.C. § 316(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB uses preponderance for invalidity issues; district courts use clear and convincing for issued patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of Litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Order temporarily suspending a Pending Civil Action, often during pendency of PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 42.122(a). Parties commonly seek stays pending PTAB resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute Claim (requirements for motion to amend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim proposed by Patent Owner to replace original claims via Motion to Amend; may propose one Substitute Claim per original claim intended to be amended and must be traceable to an original patent claim at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute Claims considered only if original replaced claim is determined unpatentable or cancelled. Proposed substitute may only narrow claim and cannot broaden it. Patent Owner must show proposed new claims are patentable at least over prior art known to Patent Owner. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.121, 42.221.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiently Final (district court judgment)
rubrics_metrics.description: District court judgment affirmed on appeal that ends litigation on the merits and leaves nothing for district court to do but execute the Judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant to estoppel and interactions with PTAB and later proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Information (timing and standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information submitted by Petitioner after filing Petition and Institution; Motion for Supplemental Information must be filed within one month of Institution and all supplemental info must be relevant to instituted claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motion after one month requires showing info could not reasonably have been obtained earlier and consideration would be in interest of justice. 37 C.F.R. § 42.123(a)-(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological Invention (CBM eligibility exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is not eligible for CBM review if it claims subject matter that as a whole recites a technological feature that is novel and unobvious and solves a technical problem using a technical solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 42.301; see Transitional Program for Covered Business Method Patents definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial (definition and time limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adversarial process where parties submit evidence, depose witnesses, and advocate regarding invalidity of a challenged patent; PTAB determines validity after Trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial period begins at Institution and continues until Final Written Decision; statutory time limit of one year after Institution with possible six-month extension for good cause. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.100, 42.2, 42.200(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified Case (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single PTAB Proceeding consisting of Joint Petitioners or Petitions after successful Motion for Joinder; multiple petitioners constitute one party and must speak with a single voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one Lead Counsel may represent multiple Joint Petitioners; consolidated filings cannot contain individual sections for different petitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity (see Invalidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterpart to Invalidity; whether patent complies with statutory prerequisites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Invalidity and Standard of Proof entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical Redundancy (redundant grounds within a petition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertion of multiple Grounds of Invalidity for a single claim based on different prior art references without explaining relative strengths/weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a ground is rejected for redundancy, petitioner is estopped from pursuing it later. Petitioners should select strongest grounds rather than vertically redundant ones.
